title: Concerto: Seqlen & Arch-aware Kernel Portfolio Balancer
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, deployable kernel-controller ("Concerto") that maintains a small portfolio of kernel implementations per model+hardware pair and dynamically balances which kernel to use per-request using a compact seqlen+arch fingerprint and a low-cost online tuner. Background: we have many one-off autotuners that pick kernels by microbenchmarks; Concerto aims to centralize and simplify decisions for mixed workloads (chat bursts, long-form prefill, mixed-precision fallbacks) so we can rely on a single service to: 1) pick a candidate kernel prior to prefill and re-evaluate during decode when token-phase shifts matter; 2) hedging: issue a speculative warmstart on a safe kernel when uncertainty is high; 3) respect latency SLOs and minimize token cost by favoring cheaper kernels when latency headroom exists. Scope and non-goals: initial scope focuses on CPU/GPU variants for attention impls we ship (blockwise, tiled, flash-attn variants) and quantized kernels (int8/4/ptq). We will not add distributed/multi-GPU placement logic in this phase. Design overview:
- Fingerprinting: concise descriptor (model-id, batch-size, seq-len, avg-prefill-len, token-phase-bucket, hw-fingerprint) encoded as 8-12 bytes for fast hashing.
- Cost model: combine offline microbench cost table (per-kernel median token throughput for common seq-len buckets) with an online EWMA latency/error term to capture drift.
- Exploration policy: epsilon-greedy with bandit-weighted softmax; exploration rate decays by profile confidence and measured SLO regret.
- Safety nets: SLA-driven timeouts + fallback path to verified stable kernel; prefill-specific safety path that forces kernels with stable KV cache semantics.
- Warmstart: when confident, launch microprobe warmstart to pre-warm kernels likely to be used in the next N tokens.
- Telemetry: emit per-request chosen kernel, chosen_score, latency, token_count, fallback_reason, probe_results.
Acceptance criteria:
- 5-10% reduction in average token cost on mixed chat/prefill traces vs static kernel policy, with <= 1% SLA violation increase.
- Tunable knobs exposed in console for risk appetite, exploration budget, and safety margins.
Implementation plan:
1) PoC library to compute fingerprint + lookup in an in-memory portfolio store (2 wks).
2) Offline profiling job to produce microbench cost table across seq-len buckets (1 wk).
3) Integrate simple bandit policy and simulate on historic traces to validate cost/regret (2 wks).
4) Implement runtime integration to return kernel token pipeline decisions and telemetry hooks (2 wks).
5) Canary rollout with synthetic traffic and A/B tests (2 wks).
Telemetry / observability:
- New metrics: kernel_choice_ratio, probe_success_rate, portfolio_confidence, per-kernel_latency_p50/p95, per-fingerprint_regret.
- Dashboards: per-model and per-region breakdown with time-based cohorting by seq-len bucket.
Safety and rollback: default to pinned stable kernel on deploy. If probe_failure_rate > 5% or p95 latency regression > 2x baseline for 10m, auto-disable exploration and revert to pinned config.
Migration considerations: start with a small set of high-variance models (conversational assistants with mixed prefill/decode patterns). Keep config JSON-backed via Console rollout to allow quick A/B.
Documentation: include quickstart for SDK, runtime hooks, and console toggles.
Engineering risks:
- Fingerprint collisions creating noisy decisions (mitigate via conservative clustering).
- Probe noise on multi-tenant GPUs; use per-GPU EWMA and cooldowns.
- Quantized kernel numerical regressions; tie to eval suite before promotion.
Dependencies: offline profiler (ENG-xyz-placeholder), console rollout API, telemetry backend updates.
Deliverables: design doc (Confluence), profiling dataset, PoC library, runtime change, canary report, console rollout config.
